- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecast tends to overshoot after sharp upward spikes in the history (e.g., after 72.62+), then gradually corrects — suggesting a lagged mean-reversion bias.
- Late forecast values (last 5–10 days) are often too high, indicating a failure to account for downward pressure or market saturation.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the 30-day forecast, particularly when history shows recent volatility or consolidation.
- When history includes a strong upward trend, model overreacts with a steep rise, then underreacts in subsequent days — suggesting a “spike-overshoot” pattern.
- Forecast does not adequately adjust for recent downward corrections in history — often fails to “reset” after a dip, leading to persistent overestimation.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of true price increases when history shows strong momentum — especially in the middle of the forecast window.
- Forecast tends to be overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then gradually adjusts — suggesting a “warm-up” bias or delayed calibration.
